about: The launch film's captions: sound descriptions plus the on-screen kinetic lines, word for word, and the time-coded audio descriptions. The single source for public/media/v2/film.en.vtt (website), film.descriptions.en.vtt and the social SRTs. The trailer (OVERRIDES 38-41; docs/FILM_SPEC.md section 24): the frames follow tools/audio/beatmap.json (100 BPM, 18 frames per beat, 72 per bar, 30 fps; the drop on f648). The three compositions (LaunchFilm 1920x1080, LaunchFilmSquare 1080x1080 and LaunchFilmVertical 1080x1920) use the same timeline, so one track serves all three.

conventions.start: first frame the caption is shown
conventions.end: first frame after the caption (exclusive); seconds = frame / 30
conventions.lines: 1 or 2 caption lines, shown together; a sound description is in square brackets and comes first, on its own line or at the start of the first line where a cue's two lines must stay together (c24: the price and its limit, OVERRIDES §46)
conventions.overlap: no two cues overlap, so the SRT needs no stacking
conventions.pace: every cue is shown for at least 1.2 s and at no more than 3 words per second
conventions.position: bottom (player default); every kinetic line on screen sits above y 918 in 16:9 and 1:1 and above y 1460 in 9:16, so captions never cover it
conventions.srt_time: HH:MM:SS,mmm, same rounding; SRT cue numbers count from 1 in this order
conventions.style: British spelling, sentence case, no exclamation marks; a kinetic line is copied exactly as it appears on screen, with its on-screen line break removed; whooshes and most clicks are not described (they carry no meaning the picture does not show)
conventions.chapters: film.chapters.vtt comes from src/content/chapters.ts (startSeconds), not from this file
conventions.descriptions: time-coded: what the picture shows in each span, read aloud by the film player's audio-description toggle; at 150 words a minute the player waits at most about 3 s for any cue and about 22 s in all (OVERRIDES 27: under 8 s each, about 100 s in all)

descriptions.text: The pebble's eyes follow the pointer, then look at you.
What did it change? An edit to dates.py waits for review; the pointer applies it.
Can I undo it? The card reads Done, with Undo this edit.
Did it run the tests? The task is held: Pebble's change isn't verified yet.
An agent shouldn't grade its own work. The pebble peeks up, leaps and hangs in silence.
It lands as the full stop of the word pebble: a small companion for your Mac. It hops onto a desktop.
In the quick chat, Pebble answers a question about a date error.
The whole Pebble window: Good to see you.
Views, not just text: a budget chart, up close.
Your model, your choice: three ways to add one.
Memory you can read and forget: a record is binned.
You set what it may do: Auto in project is chosen.
Your tests stay yours: a test change waits for you.
AgentGuard's evidence check flags files outside the task.
The task is held. AgentGuard checks the evidence. Run the tests.
Tests run in an isolated copy. Run tests.
The tests run.
42 passed. Verified. Evidence before done.
The pebble celebrates; both edits are verified.
Free and open source, Apache-2.0. No telemetry. Your keys stay in your Keychain.
The pebble lands as the full stop of pebble: a little help, right here. Free for Macs with Apple silicon. Not notarized. github.com/tohin003/Pebble. Shown with sample data.
